Playing in the tournament for the first time in 15 years, the 39-year-old lost 6-7 (4-7) 7-5 7-6 (7-5) - the first time he has been beaten by Struff in nine meetings. "I knew I needed to go for it. BBC Sport columnist Tony Pulis explains why Vincent Kompany's health scare was a reminder that management takes its toll physically and mentally A lot has changed for football managers over the past few decades but Vincent Kompany's recent health scare was a reminder it is still an all-consuming occupation that takes its toll physically and mentally. From the tragic death of Scotland manager Jock Stein after a World Cup qualifier against Wales in 1985, to the different heart issues suffered by Graeme Souness, Sir Alex Ferguson, Gerard Houllier, Joe Kinnear and Harry Redknapp down the years, I've always been aware of the dangers of my job.

Indian chef Ranji Smile opened America’s first Indian restaurant in 1901 - then became a fake prince. One hundred and twenty-five years ago, in 1901, an Indian chef opened what was almost certainly the first Indian restaurant in the US. Ranji Smile was one of the most colourful and enigmatic figures to shape the American food scene. In the summer of 1899, Smile sailed from London to New York. We know hardly anything about his origins and early life, not even his real name. "Ranji" was probably a nod to the Indian cricketing sensation KS Ranjitsinhji, then a star attraction at Test matches in Britain. "Smile" could have been an anglicisation of "Ismail".

Bigger Than Sports, a youth-operated nonprofit organization founded by Allderdice alumni Ian and Emma Waite, is working to help high school student-athletes prepare for life after athletics. The organization gained national recognition when it received the Billie Jean King Youth Leadership Award during the 2025 ESPYs. Less than 1% of high school student-athletes go on to play professional sports, leaving many uncertain about their career paths once their playing days are over. Bigger Than Sports addresses this gap by assisting student-athletes, particularly those in marginalized areas, through weekly mentorship initiatives and fireside chats with guest speakers.

Raquel Alvarez Tabernero/Shutterstock Add Engadget on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover In a casual conversation, you could maybe get away with using the acronyms GPS and GNSS interchangeably. The two are closely related, in the same way that an iPhone is a type of smartphone. GNSS stands for Global Navigation Satellite System, a broad term for any satellite navigation system, including GPS. NASA describes it as providing "autonomous geospatial positioning" because, of course, they do. The most important takeaway is that GPS, as familiar as it is to everyone, is merely a type of GNSS, specifically the United States' satellite navigation system.

The Los Angeles Dodgers have six players entering arbitration this offseason, and they need to decide how to approach them. The standard number of arbitration years is three, but players in the top 22% can earn the Super Two Exception, which lets them enter arbitration a year early and get four total years. In arbitration, a team must decide whether to tender or non-tender players by November 20th. If they are tendered, they continue to arbitration; if they are non-tendered, they become free agents. Once tendered, the team and player can agree to avoid arbitration or go to a hearing, where both sides submit a salary proposal and a third-party arbitrator rules for the player or team.

DeMonica Amerson was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis at 21. Nearly two decades later, she received devastating news. DeMonica Amerson's diagnosis of multiple sclerosis in 2001 had been a shock. No one in her family had ever had the autoimmune condition, and it had been difficult to diagnose. Doctors had first thought she had optic neuritis because her symptoms were in her eyes. Then they suspected lupus. After a spinal tap, she was diagnosed with MS. At the time, Amerson had never heard about the condition. She had just graduated from college and expected to be in the prime of her life. Instead, she had to give herself daily shots to treat the condition.

From a fake fair catch to a blind field goal lateral, these college football trick plays fooled defenses and changed games Coaches spend hours watching film to find tiny mistakes in how a team lines up. A good fake handoff, a surprise pass or a player acting like he isn't part of the play can flip a game upside down in a second. Some of these crazy calls led to famous touchdowns and huge wins. Others blew up completely, but people still talk about them anyway. The best trick plays all do the same thing, they get the defense to chase a ghost. By the time the other team figures out what is going on, the ball is already gone.

Notre Dame's Nov. 7 home game against Miami will be spotlighted on college football's preeminent pregame show. What was long assumed became official when ESPN announced that "College GameDay" will be coming to Notre Dame Saturday, Nov. 7 ahead of the No. 6 Fighting Irish's home game with No. 1 Miami . This was a game several had circled as a potential "GameDay" game, and rightfully so. Both teams began the season highly ranked, and that has held true thus far into the season. Not even a 28-24 setback to BYU on Oct. 17 – when Notre Dame was the visiting team before "GameDay" – could deny the show coming to South Bend.

The Jacksonville Jaguars were reportedly one of a few teams that reached out to the Titans about defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons In his weekly intel article, Pelissero wrote that the Jaguars were one of at least three teams to reach out to the Titans about Simmons. How far those actual conversations went remains unknown. According to Bleacher Report , Pelissero said that the Titans probably did not want to trade Simmons within the division. Simmons ended up being traded to the Chicago Bears for 2027 and 2028 first-round picks, along with a 2027 fourth-round selection.

Daniele Ghilardi is enjoying a golden moment. First the assist against Slovan, then the one against Cagliari, and finally his first league goal against Udinese on Halloween night. The number 87 spoke ... The number 87 spoke to DAZN after the match. First goal in Serie A. "I'm very happy." What does it mean to score your first goal in Serie A? "I watch it too: I kicked with all my strength. I was exhausted, I had cramps. I celebrated better than Lulli; he wasn't used to it. It took me more than two seasons… I'm happy."

Philadelphia got 21 points from Anfernee Simons off the bench Friday. The Knicks got 19 from their entire reserve group […] That comparison doesn't settle which team has the better bench. It does explain why New York's rotation deserves a closer look after the 76ers won without Jaylen Brown. Simons made five of eight three-pointers; the Knicks' reserves made two. Miles McBride scored 10 points on 4-for-8 shooting and made two threes. Tyler Kolek added four assists, while Andre Drummond grabbed six rebounds. The bench provided useful individual contributions, but it did not consistently produce enough offense to change the game.

Harter, Chief Army Reserve will lead the Terrible Towel Twirl before kickoff Sunday as part of the Steelers "Salute to Service" activities Sunday at Acrisure Stadium," Stockey wrote on X. Roethlisberger is never shy to take digs at the Browns. The future Hall of Fame quarterback still holds a grudge against the Browns for passing on him in the 2004 NFL Draft. French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of a "very high risk" of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween, as some 320,000 people nationwide took to the streets. A demonstrator holds a French flag during a demonstration against rising living costs in Paris on Saturday. Aurelien Morissard/AP hide caption PARIS — Hundreds of thousands of mostly young protesters took to the streets across France on Saturday in a third consecutive weekend of demonstrations over living costs and education. About 70,000 police and gendarmes were deployed across the country, and Paris marches were rerouted to the capital's edge. Youth-led demonstrations were also reported in Germany and Italy.

The Terps lost the fourth quarter once again in the first game of teh post-Mike Locksley era. With eight minutes left and possession of the ball, Maryland couldn't string together a drive to break the deadlock. That was the Terps' last possession of the game. Illinois soaked up the final six minutes, marching 67 yards down the field and kicking a game-winning 26-yard field goal. In the first game of the new era under interim head coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim, familiar issues arose. The Terps fell to Illinois, 20-17, and have now been outscored in the fourth quarter by 35 points this season.
